question.text: Kaveri Macro Fund, a Cat III AIF, is positioning itself as a 'Multi-Strategy Fund' in the European sense described in Section 2.6.1. What is the KEY structural difference between a Multi-Strategy Fund and a Fund-of-Funds, per the chapter?

answer.text: A Multi-Strategy Fund can only deploy a single strategy; a FoF deploys many
A Multi-Strategy Fund is regulated by the RBI, a FoF by SEBI
A Multi-Strategy Fund must be close-ended; a FoF must be open-ended
A Multi-Strategy Fund deploys multiple strategies WITHIN THE SAME FUND SCHEME, giving diversification while avoiding the double-layer of management fees that a FoF incurs

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 2.6.1 states: 'Multi-strategy Funds, on the contrary, are hedge funds which deploy multiple investment strategies, within the same fund scheme. This gives the benefit of diversification as well as controls the pay-out of management fees, by investors.' So the multi-strategy fund delivers diversification akin to a FoF but WITHIN ONE vehicle, eliminating the double-layer fee drag. The Trap: Option A inverts the definitions. Option B is wrong — both are SEBI-regulated under the AIF Regulations 2012. Option C is a fictitious constraint — Cat III AIFs can be open or close-ended, and the multi-strategy vs FoF distinction has nothing to do with tenor structure. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) tests the SAME distinction to help clients compare fee-efficient diversification options. XIX-E asks it from the manager's product-design desk.
